subject.title: exec private-LAN access fails while same user GUI/LaunchAgent succeeds

question: Should this issue be resolved as diagnostic-only exec output, or should OpenClaw pursue same-user private-LAN reachability parity for gateway-host exec?
rationale: Source inspection can prove the missing diagnostic, but allowing or intentionally blocking private-LAN exec traffic is a security and product-policy choice.

options.title: Land Diagnostic Only
options.body: Review and land the open diagnostic PR while leaving broader private-network access semantics unchanged and tracked separately.

options.title: Design Access Parity
options.body: Treat same-user GUI/LaunchAgent reachability as the product goal and require a separate security design before implementation.

options.title: Defer To Broader Trackers
options.body: Reject the diagnostic-only scope and keep the behavior under the broader private-network policy issues instead.

recommendation.title: Land Diagnostic Only
recommendation.body: Review and land the open diagnostic PR while leaving broader private-network access semantics unchanged and tracked separately.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for exec runtime design and host-routing policy is Peter Steinberger's prior work in the affected files.
